{{Short description|Mathematical concept}}
{{unreferenced|date=April 2025}}

In [[applied mathematics]], a '''damping matrix''' is a matrix corresponding to any of certain systems of linear ordinary differential equations.  A damping [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] is defined as follows.  If the system has ''n'' [[Degrees of freedom (mechanics)|degrees of freedom]] ''u''<sub>''n''</sub> and is under application of ''m'' [[Damping ratio|damping]] [[force]]s. Each [[force]] can be expressed as follows:

: <math>f_{Di}=c_{i1} \dot{u_1}+c_{i2} \dot{u_2}+\cdots+c_{in} \dot{u_n}=\sum_{j=1}^n c_{i,j}\dot{u_j} </math>

It yields in [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] form;

: <math>F_D=C \dot{U} </math>

where '''C is the damping matrix''' composed by the damping coefficients:

: <math>C=(c_{i,j})_{1\le i\le n,1\le j\le m} </math>
